notes.summary: The page asserts that every part of the figure family or of M is contained in a least saturated part, described as cosupport of cosupport and also called support. It characterizes saturated parts as supports or cosupports and says that cosup reverses inclusion in a self-correspondence of those parts. It introduces Sigma as the set of virtual supports, with realizations represented by M_sigma and family F_sigma. The written phrase family F_0 de M is retained. The final paragraph describes cosupport on Sigma by a heavily revised anti-compound and asserts arbitrary Inf as intersections and arbitrary Sup via saturation; the latter sentence continues beyond the page. These assertions have been transcribed, not proved.
math_reading_decisions: The literal equals-like mark after elles has two separate horizontal bars. It is not expanded to mêmes, even though that interpretation would complete familiar wording.
The final M in family F_0 de M has two plain uprights. H’s suggested editorial replacement with family F is rejected on the ink, while its literal M transcription is acknowledged as agreeing.

The densely revised anti-compound was inspected because its property matters mathematically. The retained alternatives replace C's uncertain older isomorph/homéo layers with possible cancellation of invo and whole-word alternatives. Involution, with possible partial cancellation, remains first among the uncertain candidates. This reading/state difference does not depend on interpreting C's permitted old-before-live notation as separate positions.

The first P has a straight stem and angular bowl without a definite lower flourish; plain P is retained among the alternatives. The second P has a lower-left curl. Two reduced F occurrences have local plain/calligraphic doubts instead of inheriting a family alphabet from context.

The cancelled capital after Sigma de has a P-like bowl and a lower-right component; family symbols with possible low indices remain alternatives. The glyph is not replaced by an expected realization symbol.
The displayed separator comma agrees with C and H. An initial R1 comparison misquoted C and was corrected during record audit; no change is counted for that comma.

workflow_note: Three fresh isolated v04 readers, whole and halves once each, followed by their own crops. Root viewed 18 existing reader crops (all15 R1, R2 14 and15, R3 17) and four new targeted crops for the unframed resp/M line, first Sigma/ens line, bottom notation, and low right space after a closing parenthesis. No whole or half page was viewed by root. R1 disclosed a clipped extreme j tail in crop06; the raised-letter target was complete. R3 disclosed that crop16 touched the bottom of the second P upright; root used the complete R1 crop14 for that occurrence. A text-only administrative audit corrected R1’s false claim that C lacked the display comma and separated H’s editorial proposed repair from counted literal differences. It confirmed the two low points as the sole missing physical group in R1’s inventory. Three returns differed in representing the worked anti-word; the final retains uncertain invo-prefix/whole-word alternatives in place of the proposed older isomorph/homéo layers. This concerns the letters and cancellation state, while convention 4 permits old-before-live notation for overprinting. No OCR, external research, compiler or mathematical proof check occurred.
